own_solution.law: Static force and torque balance give N=(m+M)g=803.6 N and H L sin(theta)=g L(m/2+Mx)cos(theta). Thus H=470.4 cot(theta) N and the total ground force is sqrt(N^2+H^2). At theta=62 degrees this is 841.624 N. Tilting the ladder q degrees toward the ground replaces theta by 62-q degrees.
assumptions: The ladder is rigid and the loaded ladder is in static equilibrium.
The smooth wall exerts only a horizontal normal force.
Static friction is sufficient to prevent slipping, as stated.
The shutter is a separate, noncontacting object beside the ladder.
The earlier experiment leaves the present stated configuration unchanged.
